questions.q: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh at the beginning of the psalm?
questions.a: The psalmist asks why Yahweh stands far off and hides in times of trouble.

questions.q: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do to the wicked?
questions.a: The psalmist asks that the wicked be caught in the schemes they have planned to use against the afflicted.

questions.q: What does the wicked man do regarding Yahweh?
questions.a: The wicked man despises Yahweh and praises those who steal from others.

questions.q: Why does the wicked man not seek God?
questions.a: The wicked man does not seek God because he is so proud.

questions.q: What does the wicked man say in his heart?
questions.a: The wicked man says in his heart that he will never be shaken and will never face distress.

questions.q: What is the wicked man always talking about?
questions.a: He constantly curses, lies, threatens others, and is always talking about harming others and doing wrong.

questions.q: What does the wicked man do to innocent people?
questions.a: He hides in ambush near the villages, murders the innocent in secret, and watches for helpless people.

questions.q: What animal is the wicked man like?
questions.a: He is like a lion that hides in a secret place and waits to seize the afflicted.

questions.q: What does the wicked man say in his heart about God?
questions.a: The wicked man says that God has forgotten, that God has hidden his face, and that God will never see.

questions.q: What does the wicked man think about his evil deeds?
questions.a: He thinks that God will not notice his evil deeds.

questions.q: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do?
questions.a: The psalmist asks Yahweh to take action to prove that he is powerful by paying attention to oppressed people.

questions.q: What does the wicked man say in his heart?
questions.a: The wicked man says in his heart that God will not seek him out.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say Yahweh does for helpless people?
questions.a: Yahweh sees the mischief done to them, and helpless people and orphans trust him as their helper.

questions.q: What does the psalmist ask Yahweh to do to the wicked?
questions.a: The psalmist asks Yahweh to make the wicked powerless and their wickedness come to nothing.

questions.q: What does the psalmist say about Yahweh’s reign?
questions.a: Yahweh is king forever and ever, and the nations have perished from his land.

questions.q: How does Yahweh respond to the afflicted?
questions.a: Yahweh hears the desires of the afflicted, strengthens their heart, attends to them, and acts justly for the orphan and oppressed.

questions.q: How does Yahweh respond to the needs of the oppressed?
questions.a: He strengthens their heart, listens to their prayer, and defends them.

commentary.text: The psalmist complains of the wickedness of the wicked.
He prays to God to appear for the relief of his people.

Verses 1–11 God's withdrawings are very grievous to his people, especially in times of trouble. We stand afar off from God by our unbelief, and then complain that God stands afar off from us. Passionate words against bad men do more hurt than good; if we speak of their badness, let it be to the Lord in prayer; he can make them better. The sinner proudly glories in his power and success. Wicked people will not seek after God, that is, will not call upon him. They live without prayer, and that is living without God. They have many thoughts, many objects and devices, but think not of the Lord in any of them; they have no submission to his will, nor aim for his glory. The cause of this is pride. Men think it below them to be religious. They could not break all the laws of justice and goodness toward man, if they had not first shaken off all sense of religion.

The psalmist speaks with astonishment, at the wickedness of the wicked, and at the patience and forbearance of God. God prepares the heart for prayer, by kindling holy desires, and strengthening our most holy faith, fixing the thoughts, and raising the affections, and then he graciously accepts the prayer. The preparation of the heart is from the Lord, and we must seek unto him for it. Let the poor, afflicted, persecuted, or tempted believer recollect, that Satan is the prince of this world, and that he is the father of all the ungodly. The children of God cannot expect kindness, truth, or justice from such persons as crucified the Lord of glory. But this once suffering Jesus, now reigns as King over all the earth, and of his dominion there shall be no end. Let us commit ourselves unto him, humbly trusting in his mercy. He will rescue the believer from every temptation, and break the arm of every wicked oppressor, and bruise Satan under our feet shortly. But in heaven alone will all sin and temptation be shut out, though in this life the believer has a foretaste of deliverance.
